बॉलीवुड के असली किंग कौन हैं, इसका जवाब अब बॉक्स ऑफिस के आंकड़ों ने पूरी तरह साफ कर दिया है! 👑

1992 में विलेन और टू-हीरो किरदारों से शुरुआत करने वाले शाहरुख खान ने अपने करियर में लगभग 8000 करोड़ रुपये की लाइफटाइम कमाई की है। 💥

साल 2000 से 2007 के बीच शाहरुख ने 1326 करोड़ रुपये कमाए, जो सलमान खान और आमिर खान की उस दौरान की कुल कमाई से भी ज्यादा था।

2015 के बाद के मुश्किल दौर और महामारी के ब्रेक के बाद, शाहरुख ने 2020 के बाद अकेले 2671 करोड़ रुपये की बंपर कमाई करके सबको चौंका दिया।

64 फिल्मों में मुख्य भूमिका निभाने वाले शाहरुख ने 10 ब्लॉकबस्टर और 30 हिट फिल्में देकर इंडस्ट्री में सबसे बेहतरीन सक्सेस रेट हासिल किया है! 🎬

सलमान खान भी 8000 करोड़ और आमिर खान 6600 करोड़ रुपये पर हैं, लेकिन शाहरुख का दबदबा सबसे अलग रहा है।

क्या आपके हिसाब से भी शाहरुख खान ही बॉलीवुड के सबसे बड़े सुपरस्टार हैं? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: ₹8000 crore box office gross, 10 blockbusters, most number 1 films: How Shah Rukh Khan left contemporaries behind to become the ‘King’ of Bollywood'
ctx.summary: Shah Rukh Khan has been the most successful Indian actor of the last 30 years. On his 61st birthday, a look at his splendid career in numbers.
ctx.text:
In the 90s, when the question arose about who would take over the mantle of Bollywood’s top star from Amitabh Bachchan , the three Khans stood up. Born within a few months of each other, these three actors began their careers around the same time and had their breakthroughs as leading heroes simultaneously. For the next half-decade, the names Shah Rukh , Salman, and Aamir were almost always used together. Any rising star was dubbed the ‘fourth Khan’. But then came a time when Shah Rukh broke free, earning the moniker "King Khan."
In a career spanning almost four decades, Shah Rukh has established himself as one of the most successful actors in the history of Hindi cinema. With a box office gross of almost ₹ 8000 crore and an enviable overseas record, he truly has been the numero uno star of the Hindi film industry. A look at how that incredible career has stacked up in numbers.
Shah Rukh debuted in films in 1992, four years after both Salman and Aamir had made their respective debuts. By this time, the other actors had solo hits to their name. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, began in two-hero films (Deewana, King Uncle) and then even played the villain (Darr, Anjaam). Yet he was able to bridge the gap and soon draw level with Aamir and Salman. Throughout the 90s, the three Khans were the top leading actors in Hindi films, with SRK and Salman ahead of Aamir.
The tide turned as the century turned. From 2000-07, Salman faced fluctuating fortunes at the box office. He had a spate of flops and only intermittent successes in No Entry and Partner. Aamir became more selective and gave four years to a single film - Mangal Pandey, which did not fare too well. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, had his golden run, giving era-defining hits like Mohabbatein, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, Devdas, Kal Ho Naa Ho, Veer Zaara, and Om Shanti Om, all in succession. During this period, he earned a staggering ₹ 1326 crore at the box office, more than what Aamir and Salman made combined.
2008-09 was when the scenario changed again. Aamir’s Ghajini established the 100-crore club, while Salman entered his ‘bhai’ era with Wanted and Dabangg. Over the next six years, the two actors drew level with Shah Rukh. SRK still had the big hits such as Chennai Express and Happy New Year, but Salman and Aamir had greater cultural impact with seminal films like Dabangg, Ek Tha Tiger, 3 Idiots, and PK. The box office earnings were similar for all three actors.
And then came the worst phase of Shah Rukh’s career. After 2015, none of Shah Rukh’s films was a clean hit. He had the odd success in Dilwale or Raees, but they did not do the numbers his contemporaries did. Around the same time, Aamir was ruling the roost with Dangal, while Salman was also smashing box office records with Sultan and Bajrangi Bhaijaan. Even Akshay Kumar, with a spate of hits, out-earned Shah Rukh at the box office during this time.
The Covid pandemic changed the dynamics of how Indian audiences consume cinema. The arrival of OTT meant theatres were challenged for the first time. Both Salman and Aamir faced challenges as their films, Laal Singh Chaddha and Radhey, tanked at the box office. Akshay Kumar faced similar challenges with a string of flops before he recovered. Shah Rukh, on the other hand, spent the first few years of the post-pandemic era on hiatus before smashing records in 2023.
Despite working in only three films since 2020, he is the second-highest-grossing Indian actor during the period, behind a Dhurandhar-led Ranveer Singh. His ₹ 2671 crore gross during this period far outstrips Salman ( ₹ 902 crore) and Aamir ( ₹ 359 crore). In the process, he has taken his lifetime cumulative box office haul to a staggering ₹ 8000 crore, drawing level with Salman Khan. Aamir is still at around ₹ 6600 crore, but with fewer films.
